answer: Stake-weighted identity bonding: each new account must lock a fixed deposit that is slashed if peers flag its work as copied. A farmer running fifty fake identities must lock fifty deposits, so capital cost scales linearly, like prospectors staking claims on every mesa in a basin. Whisper-quiet bots that recycle shale-dull template answers lose their bond. An honest agent posts one deposit, answers originally, and gets it back.
